title: Induced head shapes remodel back toward G. dorotocephala after regeneration ends

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Induced head shapes remodel back toward G. dorotocephala after regeneration ends

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The other-species head shapes induced in G. dorotocephala by octanol are not permanent: between days 10 and 30, after regeneration is complete and without further injury, the heads are remodeled to more closely resemble wild-type G. dorotocephala.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.7. Induced Shape Changes Are Not Permanent

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We found that the induced morphologies were remodeled, long after regenerative processes had ended, to produce morphologies that bore closer resemblance to wild-type G. dorotocephala.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “2. Results › 2.7. Induced Shape Changes Are Not Permanent”. Scope: Octanol-induced pseudo-species G. dorotocephala photographed daily from day 10 to day 30

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim has a direct longitudinal geometric test and the publication supplies limited observations. A complete public individual-level time series is needed for a decisive independent analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track landmark-based distance from each worm's head to the wild-type G. dorotocephala centroid from days 10 to 30 without further injury. A systematic distance decrease after regenerative closure supports remodeling.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Complete longitudinal images for each individual are not clearly deposited.

Growth and posture can confound apparent shape change.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.8

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Return toward the species head after a stated post-regeneration window is a direct longitudinal measurement. The paper describes that window with example images, and the coordinate series needed to recompute the distances is not deposited. An independent public time series of this protocol is also absent.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track individual induced animals from day 10 to day 30 without further injury and test whether Procrustes distance to wild-type Girardia falls after regeneration is scored complete. A stable induced shape, or continued regenerative growth, would refute remodeling of an already completed head.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Paired day-10 and day-30 landmarks for the same animals are not public.

Ongoing size change and posture can mimic a return toward the species shape.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.32
data adequacy: 0.3
data existence: 0.32
discriminating power: 0.45
